The official sector chart in the 2026 VHF procedure (Bijlage 2, P-S8; legally published P-S9) shows the Maas North traffic lanes north of the MN2-MN3 line within the area shaded as Sector Maas Approach (VHF 1). Distance test from the North Mole head (51 59'.67N 004 02'.84E) using Circ.67 positions (P-S1): whole scheme lies about 7.5 to 23 nm from the entrance (52 07'.1N to 52 22'.7N), inside 38 nm. Note: the statutory Rotterdam approach area (STZ Bijlage 1(f), P-S10) ends at the inner ends of the Maas TSSs (buoys MN3, MN2, MNW2, MNW3-MW4, MW5), so statutory powers (traffic instructions, navigational assistance) do not extend over the TSS; the association rests on the VTS service area (information/traffic organisation).
reporting_boundary_basis: Outside WETREP (scheme lies east of the WETREP limit line B/NL border to 52 12'N UK coast, P-S5) and all other Part I systems (P-S6). No Dutch national reporting system for the EEZ (P-S16, P-S17). The arrival report to Sector Maas Approach VHF 1 'from sea' is a VTS reporting duty (P-S8), recorded under the VTS, not as an MRS.
evidence_summary: Maas North lies in the approach covered by Rotterdam VTS Sector Maas Approach: within the stated 38 nm service area and inside the sector chart. Its southern end abuts the Pilot Maas sector / Maas Centre precautionary area. No mandatory reporting scheme applies; the VHF 1 arrival report is part of the VTS.

source_date: Port Information Guide Jan 2026; VHF procedure v2.0 Feb 2026 (Stcrt. 2026, 8272, in force 20 Feb 2026); COLREG.2/Circ.67 (in force 1 Jun 2017)
unresolved_issue: Outer VTS limit is stated as a distance ('38 nautical miles seawards'); the western end of the scheme is 4 nm inside it on a radius reading. If the 38 nm were measured along the channel the result is the same, but no coordinate boundary was found to confirm. Lower confidence: coverage rests on the port authority's 38 nm description, not a statutory boundary (the statutory Rotterdam approach area ends at the inner end of the scheme). Confirm against ALRS Vol 6 or a charted VTS limit.

vts_boundary_basis: Scheme positions (P-S1) are about 35 nm (NE end, (77) 52 05'.55N 003 06'.32E) to 41.5 nm (SW end, (75) 52 13'.42N 002 59'.03E) from the Rotterdam entrance, straddling the '38 nm seawards' Rotterdam VTS limit (P-S7); the official sector chart (P-S8) does not extend this far west. Coverage by Rotterdam VTS therefore possible for the north-eastern part but not established. Scheldt VTS area lies well to the south (P-S20).
reporting_boundary_basis: East of the WETREP limit line (at 52 05'-52 13'N the line lies near 001 50'E; scheme is at 002 56'-003 10'E) (P-S5); no other Part I system (P-S6); no Dutch EEZ reporting system (P-S16, P-S17). Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.
evidence_summary: No mandatory reporting. Possible partial overlap with the Rotterdam VTS 38 nm service area but the official chart does not show the scheme and the limit is not defined by coordinates.
source_date: COLREG.2/Circ.67 20 May 2016; Port Information Guide Jan 2026
unresolved_issue: Whether the Rotterdam VTS Sector Maas Approach outer limit (38 nm, basis of measurement undefined) includes the north-eastern part of North Hinder North. Needs ALRS Vol 6 / Dutch radio publication or a VTS boundary with coordinates.

coastal_state_s: Netherlands (IMO B-II/10); south-western part may lie in Belgian or UK EEZ waters, not verified
vts_boundary_basis: No VTS found. Scheme (51 27'-51 50'N, 002 02'-002 38'E, P-S1) is 50+ nm from the Rotterdam entrance, beyond the 38 nm Rotterdam VTS area (P-S7); it lies north of the Scheldt VTS seaward limit (about 51 23.6'-51 28.75'N between 002 19'E and 002 56'E, P-S20, 2014 folder). UK and Belgian VTS not checked beyond this.
reporting_scheme_name: West European Tanker Reporting System (WETREP)
reporting_authority: WETREP participating coastal States (per MSC.190(79) coverage points: United Kingdom, Ireland, France, Spain, Portugal, Belgium), reports to the nearest participating coastal station
reporting_boundary_basis: WETREP applies to every kind of oil tanker of more than 600 tonnes deadweight carrying heavy crude oil, heavy fuel oil or bitumen and tar (MSC.190(79) annex para 1.1): tanker-specific. Its north-eastern limit is the straight line from point 19 (51 22'25"N 003 21'52".5E) to point 20 (52 12'N UK east coast, about 001 37'E), confirmed on the chartlet (P-S5). Testing the Circ.67 positions (P-S1) against that line: all south-western and central positions (79, 80, 83, 84, 86) are 25-56' of longitude inside; the north-eastern corner positions (81, 82, 85, 87) lie within about 1-2' of the line (on it within plotting precision). Effectively the whole scheme is inside WETREP, with the NE extremity on the boundary. Outside CALDOVREP (P-S19).
evidence_summary: Inside the WETREP (VRS-0005) reporting area on the Part I boundary coordinates (near-full; NE end on the limit line). Applies to heavy-grade oil tankers only. No VTS coverage established; outside Rotterdam and (per 2014 chart) Scheldt VTS areas.
source_date: MSC.190(79) 6 Dec 2004; COLREG.2/Circ.67 20 May 2016; VTS-Scheldegebied folder v4.0 Aug 2014
unresolved_issue: WETREP boundary test is by computation from the resolution vertices (UK coast point longitude taken as about 001 37'E); the NE extremity sits on the line. Belgian/UK VTS absence not verified from a current official list; Scheldt VTS limit source is a 2014 folder.

coastal_state_s: Netherlands (IMO B-II/10); EEZ attribution not verified
vts_boundary_basis: No VTS found. Scheme (51 37'-51 44'N, 002 38'-002 47'E, P-S1) is about 50 nm from the Rotterdam entrance, beyond the 38 nm Rotterdam VTS area (P-S7), and north of the Scheldt VTS seaward limit (about 51 26'-51 29'N at these longitudes, P-S20). Dutch hydrographic guide in 2017 gave 'No particular information available' for this TSS (P-S21, historical).
reporting_scheme_name: West European Tanker Reporting System (WETREP)
reporting_authority: WETREP participating coastal States (per MSC.190(79)), reports to the nearest participating coastal station
reporting_boundary_basis: Partial. The WETREP limit line from 51 22'25"N 003 21'52".5E to 52 12'N UK east coast (P-S5) crosses the scheme: southern positions (88, 89, 90, 94, 95, 99, 100, 101) lie 1-12' of longitude inside WETREP, northern positions (92, 93, 96, 97, 98) lie 1-6' outside (P-S1 positions tested). Tanker-specific: oil tankers of more than 600 dwt carrying heavy-grade oil (MSC.190(79) para 1.1). Outside CALDOVREP (P-S19).
evidence_summary: The WETREP (VRS-0005) north-eastern limit line bisects the scheme; the southern part is inside. Heavy-grade oil tankers only. No VTS coverage established.
source_date: MSC.190(79) 6 Dec 2004; COLREG.2/Circ.67 20 May 2016
unresolved_issue: Partial WETREP coverage computed from resolution vertices, sensitive to the exact longitude of point 20 (UK coast at 52 12'N) and line type; confirm on the Ships' Routeing 2025 Part I chartlet. VTS absence not proven from an official list.

vts_authority: Directeur Centraal Nautisch Beheer Noordzeekanaalgebied (Harbour Master and VTS authority; Port of Amsterdam / Rijkswaterstaat joint nautical management)
vts_centre: Not named in the regulation (traffic centre IJmuiden is a lead)
vts_sector: Sector IJmuiden, VHF 61 (12 nm zone); IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7 is a supporting information-only channel outside the VTS sector
vts_boundary_basis: Partial coverage. The VTS area at sea is the territorial sea within a 12 nm radius of the IJmuiden breakwater heads, including the extended IJ-geul (P-S12); the statutory IJmuiden approach area uses a 12 nm arc from reference point 52 27'.9N 004 32'.1E (P-S10). IJmuiden West Inner spans 004 07'-004 20'.35E (Circ.64, P-S2). Its eastern end (e.g. (16) 52 30'.52N 004 20'.35E, about 7.6 nm) lies inside 12 nm; the 12 nm arc crosses the scheme near 004 12'.6E, so roughly the eastern 4-5 nm (less if the territorial-sea limit is tighter) is inside and the western part is outside. Partial. Pass 4: the 12 nm arc crosses the scheme at about 004 12.5E to 004 13.3E; the extended IJ-geul corridor runs between the separation zones, so the VTS area adjoins the scheme's inner edge but the lanes west of about 004 13E are outside.
reporting_boundary_basis: No Part I system (P-S6); outside WETREP (P-S5). No Dutch reporting system under STZ art. 5a or the EEZ regulation was found (P-S10, P-S17). Arrival report at 12 nm to Sector IJmuiden VHF 61 and the report to IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7 'as soon as VHF contact is possible' are VTS / port-approach duties of the same authority (P-S12), not a separate MRS.
evidence_summary: Eastern portion of IJmuiden West Inner lies inside the 12 nm VTS area of the North Sea Canal Area (Sector IJmuiden, VHF 61); western portion outside, in the information-only IJmuiden Approaches (VHF 7) area. No mandatory reporting scheme.
source_date: VTS communication regulation v2.0 10 Sep 2025 (in force 30 Sep 2025); STZ version 1 Jan 2025; COLREG.2/Circ.64 4 Dec 2012 (in force 1 Aug 2013)
unresolved_issue: Exact split point depends on whether the 12 nm is measured from the breakwater heads or the STZ reference point and on the territorial-sea limit; partial coverage itself is not in doubt. Name of the traffic centre not stated in the regulation.

vts_boundary_basis: VTS North Sea Canal Area (Port of Amsterdam directive, Q-S9) and the statutory aanloopgebied IJmuiden (Q-S10) are limited to the territorial sea within a 12 nm arc from 52°27.9'N 004°32.1'E. Computed from COLREG.2/Circ.64 coordinates (Q-S12): IJmuiden North vertex (17) 52°31.35'N 004°13.25'E is 11.98 nm from the reference point (on the arc) and all other vertices are 15.4 to 18.7 nm. The TSS therefore lies outside Sector IJmuiden and only touches its boundary. The directive's map shows a wider 'IJmuiden Aanloop' area served by IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7, which is an information-only supporting channel with no defined boundary; whether it is part of the VTS area is not established.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). No Dutch national mandatory reporting system for this area identified: STZ art. 5(1) territorial-sea entry report does not reach it because the TSS lies seaward of the 12 nm IJmuiden arc (Q-S10). The VHF 7 report to IJmuiden Approaches applies to ships bound for IJmuiden and is VTS reporting (Q-S9). Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.
evidence_summary: IJmuiden North (COLREG.2/Circ.64, implemented 1 Aug 2013) runs NNW from about 12 nm to 18.7 nm off IJmuiden. The statutory VTS North Sea Canal Area and aanloopgebied IJmuiden end at 12 nm; the TSS only touches that arc at one vertex. The IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7 information channel extends seaward but its area is not defined in the directive. No IMO or national MRS.
source_date: Q-S9 10 Sep 2025 (in force 30 Sep 2025); Q-S10 version 1 Jan 2025; Q-S12 4 Dec 2012
unresolved_issue: Whether the IJmuiden Approaches (VHF 7) service area is a defined part of VTS North Sea Canal Area and whether it covers the IJmuiden North lanes. Needs the Dutch VTS designation for IJmuiden or ALRS Vol 6 / Dutch Guide to Port Entry diagram.

vts_boundary_basis: IJmuiden West Outer (Q-S12) lies between about 003°54'E and 004°09'E, 14.1 to 15.5 nm and more from the IJmuiden reference point, so outside the 12 nm Sector IJmuiden. The VTS directive scope (a) includes 'the extended IJ-geul deep water channel' and its Appendix I map shows the IJ-geul continuing beyond 12 nm (Q-S9). In Circ.64 the West Outer separation zones are described as lying north and south of the IJmuiden-geul, with the traffic lanes outside them, so the VTS scope includes the deep-water channel the TSS flanks but not demonstrably the TSS lanes or separation zones.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). Seaward of the 12 nm IJmuiden arc, so the STZ art. 5(1) territorial-sea entry report does not apply (Q-S10). VHF 7 report to IJmuiden Approaches is VTS reporting for ships bound to IJmuiden (Q-S9). Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.
evidence_summary: The TSS flanks the extended IJ-geul beyond 12 nm. The current VTS North Sea Canal Area directive (in force 30 Sep 2025) includes the extended IJ-geul in its scope, but the TSS lanes are outside the 12 nm VTS sector and the VHF 7 information area has no defined limit. Coverage of the TSS itself is not established. No MRS.
unresolved_issue: Does the VTS area 'including the extended IJ-geul' extend to the adjoining West Outer lanes, and is IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7 a defined VTS sector? Check Dutch designation decision or ALRS Vol 6 diagram.

vts_boundary_basis: No Dutch VTS area shown to include the TSS. The statutory aanloopgebied Den Helder (Q-S10) is the Marsdiep sea area bounded by 'grote Kaap' (52°52.9'N 004°42.9'E), buoys SG, ZH, MR, NH, MG and pile 15 on Texel (53°03.7'N 004°43.3'E); the TSS north-eastbound lane's inner boundary lies at 004°17'-004°27.8'E (Q-S12). Buoy positions were not retrieved, so adjacency or overlap is not established; the evidence suggests the approach area lies inshore of the TSS. Coastguard VTMon is monitoring, not VTS (Q-S17, Q-S18).
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). Part of the TSS lies within the Dutch territorial sea (inner lane boundary about 9.5 nm off Texel). STZ art. 5(1) (Q-S10) requires ships of 300 GT or more to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea on a channel designated by ministerial regulation to the competent authority. The designation, receiving authority and practical operation were not found (Q-S11). This is not a named scheme and may be a dormant provision. Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.
evidence_summary: Off Texel (amended by COLREG.2/Circ.64, 2013) is part of the mandatory tanker route (routeing, not reporting; Q-S14). No Dutch VTS area shown to include it. A statutory territorial-sea entry reporting duty exists on paper (STZ art. 5(1)) but its channel and authority are unconfirmed.
source_date: Q-S10 version 1 Jan 2025; Q-S12 4 Dec 2012; Q-S11 version 27 Mar 2026
unresolved_issue: (1) Positions of Den Helder approach-area buoys SG, ZH, MR, NH, MG versus the TSS. (2) Whether STZ art. 5(1) is operated in practice, on which channel and to which authority (Kustwacht?). Needs the Regeling aanwijzing bevoegde autoriteiten STZ, Dutch Guide to Port Entry or ALRS Vol 6.

vts_boundary_basis: No Dutch VTS area shown to include the TSS. The statutory list of Dutch aanloopgebieden (Q-S10) contains no area off Vlieland; the nearest is aanloopgebied Brandaris, 'het zeegat van Terschelling' bounded by buoys Drawa W, ZS, TG and Stolzenfels. Buoy positions were not retrieved. VTMon is monitoring, not VTS (Q-S17).
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). IMO coordinates for B-II/13 were not retrieved, so it is not known whether any part lies in the Dutch territorial sea where STZ art. 5(1) entry reporting would apply (Q-S10); that provision's channel and authority are also unconfirmed. Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.
evidence_summary: No VTS area covering Off Vlieland found in the statutory Dutch approach-area list; only Kustwacht monitoring. The TSS is subject to the mandatory tanker route (routeing only). MRS status depends on territorial-sea extent, which was not checked.
source_date: Q-S10 version 1 Jan 2025
unresolved_issue: IMO B-II/13 coordinates (not in the opened circulars) to test territorial-sea extent and any overlap with aanloopgebied Brandaris; status of STZ art. 5(1) reporting.

vts_boundary_basis: No Dutch VTS area shown to include the TSS: the statutory aanloopgebieden (Q-S10) are all inshore port approaches and none is off Vlieland. Kustwacht VTMon is monitoring, not VTS (Q-S17, Q-S18). This is not treated as proof of absence because the Dutch VTS designations for offshore waters were not retrieved.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). Territorial-sea extent not checked (IMO coordinates not retrieved), so the applicability of STZ art. 5(1) is not resolved. Pass 4: Scheepvaartreglement territoriale zee art. 5(1) requires ships of 300 GT or more, or carrying dangerous goods, to report before entering the Dutch territorial sea; this is made as the VTS or approach-area arrival report and is not a separate ship reporting system.
evidence_summary: Offshore Dutch TSS on the northern (mandatory tanker) route. No VTS or MRS association established; only Coastguard monitoring and route advice. The Coastguard's container-ship advice (Q-S19) promotes the northern route but is not a reporting scheme.
source_date: Q-S10 version 1 Jan 2025
unresolved_issue: IMO B-II/13 coordinates; whether any Dutch VTS or reporting duty applies offshore of the approach areas. The Coastguard container-ship advice (Q-S19) directs large container ships to the northern route via TSS East Friesland; whether the MSC 109 recommendation carries any reporting element is not established.

vts_authority: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung des Bundes (GDWS / WSA Weser-Jade-Nordsee)
vts_sector: German Bight Traffic (VHF 16/79/80; statutory Inner German Bight = VHF 80 coverage area)
vts_boundary_basis: Partial coverage. AnlBV Anhang chart (Q-S2), the statutory definition of the Inner German Bight, is the area covered by German Bight Traffic VHF channel 80. On it, the area boundary crosses TSS Terschelling-German Bight at about 006°16'-006°22'E (estimated from the chart graticule), so the German section east of there is inside. AnlBV Nr. 5.1 states traffic there is monitored under maritime traffic safety and Nr. 3.1 requires reports to 'Verkehrszentrale German Bight Traffic' (Q-S1). ELWIS lists German Bight Traffic as a VTS sector of Verkehrszentrale Wilhelmshaven covering the sea area between Ems and Elbe (Q-S3). WSA states Wilhelmshaven monitors the inner German Bight from Borkum to Helgoland (Q-S6). The Dutch western section (to about 006°16'E) is not shown to be in any VTS.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). German part: AnlBV Nr. 3.1 entry report (ships over 300 GT, at 007°10'E or 54°20'N) and SeeSchStrO § 58 reports are made to German Bight Traffic, a VTS, so they are recorded as VTS reporting, not a separate MRS (Q-S1, Q-S20). Dutch part: STZ art. 5(1) territorial-sea entry reporting may apply where the lanes enter the Dutch territorial sea, but its operation is unconfirmed (Q-S10).
evidence_summary: Statutory chart and AnlBV place the German section of TSS Terschelling-German Bight inside the German Bight Traffic (VHF 80) Inner German Bight area. German Bight Traffic is a VTS sector of Verkehrszentrale Wilhelmshaven established under SOLAS V/12. Coverage is partial; the Dutch section is not covered by any VTS shown. Coastguard wave-height advice is voluntary route advice (Q-S19).
source_date: Q-S2 BGBl. I 2005 p. 2297 (current Anhang); Q-S1 current consolidation accessed 29 Sep 2026; Q-S5 18 Aug 2017
unresolved_issue: Precise boundary longitude (chart-scale estimate about 006°16'-006°22'E, 2005 chart; TSS geometry since amended). Whether German Bight Traffic's western area (VHF 79, lead Q-S21) extends further west than the VHF 80 Inner German Bight. Status of Dutch STZ art. 5(1) reporting and Brandaris approach-area buoy 'TG' position.

vts_authority: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung des Bundes (GDWS / WSA Weser-Jade-Nordsee)
vts_sector: German Bight Traffic (VHF 80 area / Inner German Bight)
vts_boundary_basis: Partial coverage. AnlBV Nr. 3.1 names the TSS and requires ships entering the Inner German Bight from the west to report to German Bight Traffic at 007°10'E, whether or not they use GBWA (Q-S1). On the AnlBV Anhang chart (Q-S2) the Inner German Bight (VHF 80 area) boundary runs north-south at about 007°18'E and crosses only the easternmost few miles of the TSS; the TSS's main length to the west lies outside. So coverage by German Bight Traffic is partial (eastern end). The western part lies in the outer German Bight, where ELWIS lists Verkehrszentrale Cuxhaven 'Äußere Deutsche Bucht' with sector German North Sea Traffic (Q-S3), but no boundary shows it includes the TSS. Pass 4: AnlBV Nr. 3.1 requires a report to German Bight Traffic at 007 10E, west of the statutory VHF 80 boundary (about 007 19E); a commercial source (findaport, lead only) gives a German Bight Traffic VHF 79 reporting point at buoy GW/B (54 10.42N 006 54.00E) on this TSS. Coverage probably extends further west than recorded; not confirmed by a Tier 1 source.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). AnlBV Nr. 3.1 report at 007°10'E (over 300 GT) is made to German Bight Traffic (VTS reporting, national statute). AnlBV Nr. 6 (mandatory use of GBWA by large tankers) and the IMO mandatory tanker route (Q-S14) are routeing, not reporting, measures.
evidence_summary: GBWA is named in AnlBV Nr. 3.1 and Nr. 6. Only its eastern end lies inside the statutory German Bight Traffic (VHF 80) area; most of its length is in the outer German Bight EEZ. VTS only on a partial-coverage basis. German North Sea Traffic (Cuxhaven) is a lead for the western part.
source_date: Q-S2 BGBl. I 2005 p. 2297; Q-S1 current consolidation accessed 29 Sep 2026
unresolved_issue: Whether German North Sea Traffic (VTS Centre Cuxhaven, 'Äußere Deutsche Bucht') has a defined area including the GBWA lanes (BSH VTS Guide Germany 2026 section C5.1 not freely available). Current IMO geometry of GBWA against the 2005 chart boundary (about 007°18'E) and the 007°10'E reporting meridian.

vts_authority: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung des Bundes (GDWS / WSA Weser-Jade-Nordsee)
vts_sector: German Bight Traffic (VHF 80 area / Inner German Bight)
vts_boundary_basis: AnlBV Nr. 8 places the pilot transfer position 'im Verkehrstrennungsgebiet "Jade Approach"' within the Inner German Bight outside the territorial sea (Q-S1). The Inner German Bight is statutorily the German Bight Traffic VHF 80 coverage area (Q-S2); on that chart the Jade Approach lies well inside the area (east of the about 007°18'E boundary, south-west of Helgoland) and adjacent to the territorial sea boundary. Nr. 5.1: traffic monitored under maritime traffic safety. Consistent with WSA 'inner German Bight from Borkum to Helgoland' (Q-S6).
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). AnlBV Nr. 3.1 and SeeSchStrO § 58 reports go to German Bight Traffic/Jade Traffic (VTS reporting).
evidence_summary: Statute names the Jade Approach TSS as lying in the Inner German Bight, which the statutory chart defines as the German Bight Traffic VHF 80 area; the whole TSS lies inside that area on the chart. VTS only.
source_date: Q-S2 BGBl. I 2005 p. 2297; Q-S1 current consolidation accessed 29 Sep 2026
unresolved_issue: Coverage 'full' relies on the 2005 statutory chart; Jade Approach geometry may have been amended since (IMO instrument not retrieved), but any amendment near 54°N 007°30'-007°45'E would remain well inside the area.

vts_authority: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung des Bundes (GDWS / WSA Weser-Jade-Nordsee)
vts_sector: German Bight Traffic (VHF 80 area / Inner German Bight); Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic adjoins from Tonne Elbe
vts_boundary_basis: On the AnlBV Anhang chart (Q-S2), the Elbe approach TSS (near 54°00'N 008°05'E on the 2005 chart) lies deep inside the German Bight Traffic VHF 80 coverage arc and east of the about 007°18'E boundary. The GDWS SeeSchStrO Bekanntmachung (Q-S7) makes Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic responsible from Tonne Elbe inward, with outbound vessels reporting at Tonne Elbe to German Bight Traffic on VHF 80, so the TSS seaward of Tonne Elbe falls to German Bight Traffic. ELWIS/WSA describe Cuxhaven as covering the 'Elbeansteuerung' (Q-S3, Q-S8). Both are sectors of the German coastal VTS; the TSS is covered either way.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers this area: nearest are WETREP (VRS-0005), whose North Sea limit runs from the Belgium/Netherlands border to the UK east coast at 52°12'N (Q-S15), and CALDOVREP (VRS-0008, Dover Strait). SeeSchStrO § 58 reports at Tonne Elbe (Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic inbound VHF 71; German Bight Traffic outbound VHF 80) and AnlBV Nr. 3.1 are VTS reporting (Q-S7, Q-S1, Q-S20).
evidence_summary: The Elbe approach TSS lies inside the statutory German Bight Traffic VHF 80 area, seaward of the Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic sector boundary at Tonne Elbe. VTS only; the exact split between German Bight Traffic and Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic at the TSS's east end depends on the Tonne Elbe position versus current TSS geometry.
source_date: Q-S2 BGBl. I 2005 p. 2297; Q-S7 BAnz AT 31.01.2014 B7 (amended to 2024, Nr. 29.1 not seen amended)
unresolved_issue: Current IMO Elbe approach geometry versus Tonne Elbe (sector hand-over), and whether later amendments moved the Cuxhaven Elbe Traffic limit (the prior lead cited Nordergründe-Nord). This affects the sector split, not the VTS association.

tss_name: In the approaches to the River Humber
vts_authority: Associated British Ports, Humber Estuary Services (Statutory Harbour Authority)
vts_sector: Humber Approaches (VHF 14, seaward to No. 4A Clee Ness Light Float meridian)
vts_boundary_basis: VTS Humber seaward limit (Q-S16): Easington Church (53°39.02'N 000°06.90'E) 086° to 53°40'N 000°30'E, 180° to 53°30'N 000°30'E, 262° to Donna Nook (53°28.40'N 000°09.23'E). All TSS vertices (Q-S13) lie west of 000°30'E (maximum 000°22.95'E) and south of the northern line (point 36 at 53°38.70'N versus the line at about 53°39.6'N). vts_boundary_basis: No official source found that places the TSS in a declared VTS area. The Irish Coast Guard states it monitors traffic in the Tuskar/Fastnet TSS (S-S9), but does not describe this as a VTS. reporting_scheme_name: West European Tanker Reporting System (WETREP)
reporting_authority: Irish Coast Guard: MRCC Dublin (communications also via MRSC Valentia and MRSC Malin Head); other WETREP coastal States for their sectors
reporting_boundary_basis: MSC.190(79) para 2.1: the WETREP polygon runs 56°30'N 012°W - 54°40'41"N 015°W - 50°56'45"N 015°W - 48°27'N 006°25'W, with the inner closing point 21 on the Irish east coast (52°10'N 006°22'W). At Fastnet's longitude (c. 009°36'W) the southern boundary line lies near 49°23'N, about 2° south of the TSS, so the TSS (off Fastnet Rock, c. 51°18'-51°23'N) is wholly inside. Applies only to oil tankers >600 dwt carrying heavy crude, heavy fuel oil or bitumen/tar; WETREP does not name the TSS. Pass 4: MSC.190(79) annex para 6.2.1 names 'Off Fastnet Rock' among the TSS in the WETREP area. Applies to oil tankers over 600 dwt carrying heavy grade oil.
evidence_summary: Inside the WETREP (VRS-0005) mandatory reporting area (tankers with heavy grade oil only). The Irish Coast Guard monitors traffic in the TSS, but no declared VTS area was found covering it.
source_date: MSC.190(79) 2004-12-06 (in force 2005-07-01); gov.ie IRCG page modified 2025-07-08; accessed 2026-09-29
unresolved_issue: Whether Irish Coast Guard monitoring of the Fastnet TSS amounts to a VTS (no official VTS designation found); no official list of Irish VTS consulted to prove absence. TSS coordinates taken from a search snippet only (lead only); inclusion in WETREP rests on the boundary geometry, not on those coordinates.

No official source shows VTS coverage, and no official complete list of Panamanian VTS shows that there is none.

vts_boundary_basis: NGA Pub. 125 links the Callao TSS to TRAMAR, the Callao maritime traffic control office. All vessels report at 20, 10 and 4 miles from Isla San Lorenzo and at the Outer Fairway Buoy, which spans the TSS (Parts I to III lie about 2 to 4 nm off Isla San Lorenzo and the port). Pub. 125 does not call TRAMAR a VTS. A Peruvian Navy VTS at Callao (Wärtsilä Navi-Harbour, operating by 2024) is shown only in supplier material. No official source gives its name, area or coverage of the TSS.
reporting_authority: Capitanía de Puerto del Callao (TRAMAR), DICAPI (per NGA Pub. 125)
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system applies (only GALREP, VRS-0019, Galapagos). NGA Pub. 125 (Tier 3, corrected to 27 Aug 2026) makes reports to TRAMAR mandatory for all vessels and ties them explicitly to the TSS. No Peruvian statutory or DICAPI source for the requirement was obtained. The requirement cannot be classed as a formally named national MRS. If TRAMAR is the Callao VTS, it is VTS reporting and not a separate MRS. Recorded as Unresolved, not Yes.
evidence_summary: IMO B-VIII/6 (COLREG.2/Circ.48 Annex 4, in force 1 Dec 2000): three parts, a precautionary area and an ATBA off Callao. NGA Pub. 125 says: 'An IMO-adopted Traffic Separation Scheme (TRAMAR) ... All vessels must report to TRAMAR on VHF channel 16' at 20, 10 and 4 miles from Isla San Lorenzo. There is strong evidence that a traffic control or VTS function covers the TSS, but it is Tier 3 (foreign) evidence and does not name a VTS. The DICAPI 2025/2026 Callao anchorage resolutions do not mention TRAMAR or a VTS. The supplier case study and a 2023 naval journal article (404) point to a new 'VTS Callao'. They are lead-only sources. It cannot be classified as VTS until a DICAPI source defines the service and its area.
source_date: COLREG.2/Circ.48 1 Jun 2000; Pub. 125 17th ed 2025 corrected to 27 Aug 2026; RD 348-2026 8 Jun 2026; Wärtsilä case study 17 Apr 2025
unresolved_issue: Obtain a DICAPI resolution or HIDRONAV radio aids entry establishing 'VTS Callao' / TRAMAR. It should give the official name, service area, VHF channels and participation. Confirm whether it covers all three TSS parts and whether the TRAMAR reports are part of that VTS or a separate national scheme.
